prompt: Stage 5-1, level 8 with 62 gold, 40 HP, 1-loss streak. Your board is 2-star Sett, Malphite, Aphelios and Sivir with items. Two players are already level 9 and two more will be next round. Level 9 costs 20 gold (5 purchases). Do you level now or hold 50 and roll at 8 for a 3-star?

options.label: Level 9 now, then roll the remaining ~40 for Ashe or Maokai and a 9th unit
Stay 8, hold 50, and roll at 5-2 for the 3-star Aphelios (you have 7 copies)
Hold 50 this round and level 9 at 5-2 with more gold

explanation:
At 40 HP in stage 5 a loss costs 15+ HP, so you have two losses left and no time to wait for a better round. The lobby is capping to 9 around you, which means your 8-unit board loses to boards with a 5-cost and a ninth unit even with your 2-stars. Level 9 now moves 5-cost odds from 3% to 15% and there is already an Ashe in the shop; buying her on the way through and rolling 40 gold at 9 gives you a realistic shot at a second 5-cost or a 2-star Ashe over the next two rounds. That is the upgrade path that keeps pace with the lobby.

The 3-star Aphelios is a trap here: two more copies out of a pool of 10, with 7 in your hands, leaves 3 in the entire pool, and level-8 4-cost odds at 30% still make each specific copy a roughly 10%-per-slot event. You would likely burn all 60 gold and stay at 8 units. Holding for 5-2 costs 5 interest but risks a 15-HP loss for a board that does not improve; at 40 HP that trade is wrong.
principle: In stage 5 the level decides the cap; with two losses left, buy the level before the loss.
commonMistake: Chasing a 3-star 4-cost with 3 copies left in the pool because "I already have 7".
